prayerExcerpt.en-US: The cross is the ladder by which we must ascend to heaven.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: A cruz é a escada pela qual devemos subir ao céu.

meta.face: Three clearly different Romans. CYRIACUS (centre), about forty, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a light-olive complexion and a FULL, SOFT, SQUARE face — a broad, smooth forehead, LARGE, luminous hazel eyes set WIDE apart under dark, arched brows, a SHORT, WIDE nose with rounded nostrils, full cheeks, a WIDE, full-lipped mouth, a squared, softly padded chin; short, thick, straight dark-brown hair; a serene, upward gaze. LARGUS (left), about sixty: a LONG, HEAVY face whose features DROOP — long ear lobes, a big, fleshy nose, heavy, pouched dark eyes under drooping grey brows, loose cheeks, a grey-stubbled jaw, thin grey hair combed forward; a patient, weary kindness. SMARAGDUS (right), about twenty-five: a NARROW, FOX-LIKE face — a sharp, slightly upturned nose, narrow, slanting green eyes, high thin brows, a pointed chin, a light first beard along the jaw, wavy reddish-brown hair; an eager look.
meta.basis: No likeness survives; beyond their names, martyrdom and burial on the Via Ostiensis on 8 August, nothing is certain (Wikipedia). The book calls Cyriacus a deacon under Marcellinus and Marcellus, and its engraving shows him in a dalmatic; the three faces are ours.
